title: Text and Data Tools Learning Project
prerequisites: Completion of Study Days 01-12: Python strings, dicts, lists, file handling, basic terminal CLI usage, and test-driven development fundamentals.
requirements: 1. Command Interface: Implement a runnable CLI (e.g. `python3 projects/text_tools/cli.py`) supporting `--input`, `--stats`, `--split`, `--output-dir`, `--seed`, `--encoding`, and `--errors` flags.

2. Corpus Statistics: Ingest a text corpus and compute total character counts, total token counts, vocabulary size (unique tokens), character frequency distributions, token frequency tables, and min/max/average token lengths.

3. Deterministic Splitting: Split input records into train, validation, and test subsets based on configurable ratios (default: 0.8, 0.1, 0.1) using an inspectable fixed seed to guarantee byte-for-byte reproducibility across runs. Byte-for-byte reproducibility is scoped to the same input bytes, the same ratios, the same seed, the same decoding options, and this implementation/environment -- not across different implementations or platforms.

4. Provenance & Split Manifest: Generate `manifest.json` recording the source path, the SHA256 of the original input bytes, file size, the input decoding policy (encoding, error handling, newline normalization), seed, split ratios, split sample counts, per-split SHA256 hashes, system environment, and explicit verification that the assigned record indices are pairwise disjoint. The manifest records and checks index identity; by itself it does not enforce how consumers use the splits or prove that no duplicate content exists.

5. Robust Edge Case Resilience: Succeed (exit 0) on empty input, repeated tokens, multilingual Unicode, and `--errors replace` recovery; fail with a descriptive message and non-zero exit on missing files, strict-mode undecodable bytes, non-finite or out-of-range split ratios, and input/output path collisions.

predictions.question: If you process `data/names.txt` (32,033 names), what shape do you predict for the token frequency distribution compared to the character frequency distribution?
predictions.guidance: Predict which characters appear most frequently (vowels vs consonants) and whether individual names repeat or remain largely unique in the dataset.

predictions.question: What happens if you execute splitting twice with the exact same seed (e.g. `--seed 42`) versus with two different seeds (`--seed 42` vs `--seed 99`)?
predictions.guidance: Predict whether the SHA256 checksums of `train.txt`, `val.txt`, and `test.txt` will match or diverge, and why deterministic seeds are essential for reproducible machine learning.

predictions.question: What is the difference between string length (`len(s)`) and byte length (`len(s.encode('utf-8'))`) for English text versus Chinese/Japanese characters?
predictions.guidance: Predict memory and tokenizer buffer implications when transitioning from single-byte ASCII to variable-length UTF-8 encodings.

worked_examples.title: Example 1: Computing Statistics on names.txt
worked_examples.expected_output_summary: Produces valid JSON with total_chars=228145, total_tokens=32033, vocab_size=29494 (unique tokens, not total occurrences), with 'a' and 'e' as the most frequent letters in char_frequencies; the newline character also ranks among the top characters (second, after 'a').

worked_examples.title: Example 2: Deterministic 80/10/10 Splitting
worked_examples.expected_output_summary: Illustrative output: the first line captures and validates the absolute repository, CLI, and corpus paths BEFORE changing directory, then creates two invocation-owned private directories. From the unrelated private working directory it invokes the real CLI with absolute paths only and a private --output-dir; ls lists train.txt (25,626 lines), val.txt (3,203 lines), test.txt (3,204 lines), stats.json, vocab.json, and manifest.json. Verified in bash; this is ordinary process isolation, not an OS security sandbox, and is not claimed for other shells or platforms. The whole recipe runs in a subshell, so the caller's working directory is preserved for the next example.

worked_examples.title: Example 3: Handling Malformed Encoding with Recovery
worked_examples.command: WORKDIR=$(mktemp -d) && printf 'ok line \377 bad\n' > "$WORKDIR/corrupt.txt" && python3 -c "import sys; assert b'\xff' in open(sys.argv[1],'rb').read()" "$WORKDIR/corrupt.txt" && python3 projects/text_tools/cli.py --input "$WORKDIR/corrupt.txt" --stats --errors replace
worked_examples.expected_output_summary: Illustrative: printf octal \377 writes the literal 0xFF byte into a file inside the invocation-owned directory, and the embedded python assert verifies that byte is present. With --errors replace the CLI decodes it as U+FFFD and exits 0; a separately labeled strict variant (same input, --errors strict) fails non-zero with a descriptive UnicodeDecodeError. Verified in bash and in sh linked to bash; dash is not installed here, so no dash-specific result is claimed, and this is evidence for the executed shell only.

exercises.title: Corpus Statistics and Frequency Counter
exercises.prompt: Implement `analyze_text(text: str)` in `projects/text_tools/core.py`. Return total characters, total tokens, unique vocabulary size, character distribution, and frequency dictionaries.
exercises.check: Verify on a small sample sentence (e.g. 'the cat sat on the mat') that token counts and frequencies match hand-calculated numbers.

exercises.title: Seeded Deterministic Train/Val/Test Splitting
exercises.prompt: Implement `compute_splits(lines, train_ratio, val_ratio, test_ratio, seed)`. Use a seeded pseudo-random generator to partition line indices into mutually disjoint sets.
exercises.check: Verify that `len(set(train_indices) & set(val_indices)) == 0` (index-level disjointness) and that two runs with `--seed 42` yield identical outputs; also state your duplicate/sample policy -- whether identical record content may appear in more than one split, and whether that is acceptable for your data.

exercises.title: Data Provenance Manifest Generation
exercises.prompt: Construct `manifest.json` containing SHA256 checksums of the input corpus and each output split, the seed, ratios, sample counts, and environment details.
exercises.check: Verify manifest file matches JSON schema and accurately records runtime environment.

exercises.title: Edge Case Resilience
exercises.prompt: Add error handling for empty input, non-existent files, invalid split ratio sums, and decoding errors with `--errors strict|replace|ignore`.
exercises.check: Run test suite from an isolated working directory with process isolation.

reference_feedback.architecture_notes: Separating calculation (`core.py`) from presentation (`cli.py`) creates deep modules that can be reused by future projects (e.g. tokenizer training in Makemore and NanoGPT). Avoid storing duplicate entire corpora in memory when processing large files.
common_pitfalls: Omitting random seeds, leading to differing data splits on every run and invalidating experimental comparison.
Treating index-disjoint splitting as proof of no leakage: identical record content can still span splits unless the declared sample/duplicate policy permits it.
Assuming 1 character equals 1 byte, which breaks on CJK and emoji Unicode sequences.
Crashing on empty input files due to unhandled ZeroDivisionError in average length calculations.

debugging_cases.title: Silent Data Leakage
debugging_cases.symptom: Model achieves 99.8% validation accuracy during training but fails completely in production.
debugging_cases.root_cause: Records were allocated by index without a declared duplicate policy: index overlap was 0, but identical record content still appeared in multiple splits (e.g. ten identical 'echo' lines share one value across train/val/test; in names.txt at seed 42, 424 unique values appear in both train and val).
debugging_cases.remediation: Verify index disjointness (`len(set(train_indices) & set(val_indices)) == 0`) to confirm allocation integrity, and separately report unique-value intersections across splits. Shuffling alone does not remove duplicate content; repeated independent values are legitimate only if the declared sample/duplicate policy allows them.

debugging_cases.title: UnicodeDecodeError on Multilingual Input
debugging_cases.symptom: CLI crashes with `UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 12`.
debugging_cases.root_cause: File contains non-UTF-8 bytes or was saved with legacy encodings (GBK, Shift-JIS, ISO-8859).
debugging_cases.remediation: Expose `--encoding` and `--errors` flags, report clear diagnostic errors to stderr, and provide graceful `--errors replace` fallback.

debugging_cases.title: ZeroDivisionError on Empty Input
debugging_cases.symptom: CLI crashes with `ZeroDivisionError: division by zero` when processing empty files.
debugging_cases.root_cause: Average token length calculation divided by `total_tokens` without checking if `total_tokens == 0`.
debugging_cases.remediation: Guard against zero division: return `avg_token_length = 0.0` when `total_tokens == 0`.

debugging_cases.title: Non-Deterministic Splits Across Environments
debugging_cases.symptom: Colleague runs the same script with the same seed but gets different train/val splits.
debugging_cases.root_cause: The pipeline iterated an unordered `set` (or built a dict from one) before shuffling: set iteration order varies with `PYTHONHASHSEED` across runs. A dict keeps its insertion order deterministically within a run -- hash randomization does not reorder an otherwise identically constructed dict -- but a dict built from an unordered source inherits that source's unstable order.
debugging_cases.remediation: Operate strictly on ordered lists with explicit index permutation (`indices = list(range(n)); rng.shuffle(indices)`); if input must pass through an unordered container, re-establish a fixed order (e.g. sorting) first.

independent_mastery_checks.prompt: Without AI assistance, explain why data leakage between training and validation sets undermines model evaluation, and demonstrate how to mathematically check for leakage.
independent_mastery_checks.criteria: Learner clearly articulates optimistic evaluation bias, demonstrates index-level intersection validation `len(set(train_indices) & set(val_indices)) == 0` on the public list-valued result, and distinguishes index disjointness from duplicate-content overlap.

independent_mastery_checks.prompt: Write a pure Python deterministic partitioning function from scratch without using scikit-learn or external packages.
independent_mastery_checks.criteria: Code uses `random.Random(seed)` with list indexing, correctly calculates boundary slice indices, guarantees no overlapping index assignments, and states its duplicate/sample policy for repeated record content.

independent_mastery_checks.prompt: Explain the difference between character count, Unicode code points, and UTF-8 byte length for English, Chinese, and emoji characters.
independent_mastery_checks.criteria: Learner accurately distinguishes code points, UTF-8 byte length, and displayed grapheme sequences: 'A' is 1 code point/1 byte, '中' is 1/3, '😀' is 1/4, '❤️' is 2/6 (heart + variation selector), '👍🏽' is 2/8 (emoji + skin-tone modifier), and a family ZWJ sequence can be 7/25 -- byte length per displayed glyph is not constant.

agent_assisted_checks.prompt: Direct an AI agent to implement the CLI argument parser and test cases, then conduct a critical code review on the agent's pull request diff.
agent_assisted_checks.criteria: Learner critically reviews the agent's diff with real edge-case checks (e.g. division by zero, non-zero exit codes on failure) and recorded evidence. If a genuine omission or defect is found, the learner directs the agent to fix it; if the implementation is already correct, the learner records the checks run, the evidence that no defect was found, and the limits of that testing -- never inventing a bug.

agent_assisted_checks.prompt: Use an AI agent to generate automated property-based test cases for string edge cases while verifying sandbox isolation.
agent_assisted_checks.criteria: Learner verifies that generated tests execute in an isolated environment without writing outside temporary directories.

acceptance_checklist.label: CLI command interface executes via `python3 projects/text_tools/cli.py` with standard flags.
Corpus statistics accurately calculate character count, token count, vocab size, and frequency tables.

Deterministic splitting reproduces split-file bytes within the tested environment only when the same original input bytes (yielding the same ordered decoded records), ratios, seed, decoding/newline policy, and implementation/runtime/platform are held fixed; manifest timestamps differ and cross-version/OS byte-identity is not guaranteed.

Zero overlap of assigned record indices across train, val, and test is verified and documented in `manifest.json`; the declared duplicate/sample policy states whether repeated record content is permitted.
Empty input, repeated values, Unicode (CJK/emojis), missing files, and malformed encoding are handled robustly.
All tests run from a clean temporary environment with complete process isolation.
